turns.text: Survey recent work on hydrostatic mass bias in galaxy clusters. Use the hydrodynamics emulator to predict CGD (gas density) and CTP (temperature) profiles at two redshifts and discuss how profile shape evolution affects mass reconstruction.

**Survey** — 52 tools on 5 servers, 7 read-only probes, 14 papers found.

Simulations and observations agree that X-ray/SZ hydrostatic (HSE) masses come out too low. Simulations typically give b of about 0.1-0.2, mostly from non-thermal pressure (turbulence, bulk motions, rotation) and from mergers. FLAMINGO (2409.07849) finds the median bias grows from about -0.1 on group scales to about -0.2 on cluster scales. At fixed true mass, HSE masses rise with redshift for groups and fall for clusters, and the scatter grows with redshift. The bias also depends on feedback strength and on how well the density and temperature profiles are fitted. Merger studies (1112.3659, 2511.10730) show the bias changes over time, with transient spikes after major mergers. Earlier simulation work (1306.3993, 1308.6589, 1404.4636) finds the non-thermal pressure fraction rising with radius and redshift, because higher-z clusters are accreting faster. Observationally, X-COP clusters out to R200 (1805.00035, 1805.00034, 2112.07554) show low non-thermal support (about 6% at R500) and a small bias in relaxed systems. Profile shape matters because the HSE mass depends on the log-slopes d ln n_gas/d ln r and d ln T/d ln r, not on amplitudes. Simba shows feedback changes gas-density slopes as a function of mass and redshift (2409.05815), so slope evolution between redshifts feeds directly into how the bias evolves. Warning: none of my tools (search_arxiv, web_search, search_arxiv_abstracts, get_arxiv_metadata) is a hydrodynamics emulator, and my searches found no tool or paper using the names CGD/CTP, so I could not produce the requested profile predictions.

Quantities worth checking: Log-slopes d ln n_gas/d ln r and d ln T/d ln r at 0.5, 1 and 2 R500c, at both redshifts; M_HSE(<r) = -(k_B T r / G mu m_p)(dln n/dln r + dln T/dln r), compared with the emulator's true M500c, giving b_HSE at each redshift; Change in b_HSE between the two redshifts at fixed true mass, compared with FLAMINGO (bias grows in magnitude with z on cluster scales); Profiles scaled self-similarly (n/E(z)^2, T/T500) to separate shape evolution from plain amplitude scaling; Pressure-gradient contribution compared with the T(R500) contribution to the scatter; Sensitivity of the bias to the choice of fitting function (e.g. Vikhlinin density and temperature models) and to fit residuals.

**Plan** — 4 lines of investigation:
1. Use the HACC hydro emulator to predict CGD (gas density) and CTP (temperature) profiles at two redshifts for a fiducial parameter set. Derive the log-slopes d ln n_gas/d ln r and d ln T/d ln r at 0.5, 1 and 2 R500c, and from them a hydrostatic mass estimate and b_HSE at each redshift. — This is the direct deliverable. The HSE mass depends on the logarithmic slopes of the density and temperature profiles, so the emulator's profile shapes at two epochs show how shape evolution alone shifts the reconstructed mass.
2. Build a cited literature baseline on hydrostatic mass bias and its redshift and feedback dependence, with quotable numbers to compare against the emulator results. — The task asks for a survey. The interpretation of d-01 needs verified published values: the FLAMINGO b(z, M) trends, the X-COP non-thermal fraction and universal profiles, the Nelson et al. non-thermal pressure fits, and the Simba density-slope evolution.
3. Test how robust the profile-shape-driven bias evolution is to the emulator's astrophysical (feedback) and cosmological parameters. Estimate the non-thermal pressure fraction needed to reconcile M_HSE with the true mass. — The bias depends on feedback through the gas-density slopes. Varying the emulator parameters checks whether the redshift trend found in d-01 is generic or tied to one model, and connects it to the FLAMINGO and Simba feedback results.
4. Test the mass dependence of the profile-slope-driven HSE bias, groups versus clusters, at both redshifts. This lets the FLAMINGO result (2409.07849) of groups rising and clusters falling with z be compared directly. — The FLAMINGO comparison listed in the brief is mass-dependent. A single fiducial mass bin cannot test whether the redshift trend differs in sign or size between group and cluster scales. None of the current directions varies mass. (added by the critic)
Critic's view: revise — The calls do not fit the 13-call budget. Planned calls are list_observables, describe_parameters, 4 predict_observable, list_agent_files, up to 4 load_table_data, preview, describe, 2 overlays and 2 plot_prediction, which is about 18. Cut preview and describe_dataset, use one plot_prediction or none, and load only when outputs are files. Leave about 2 calls in reserve.; b_HSE needs a true mass, and that has to come from the emulator definition, not from assumption. Check whether CGD and CTP are stacked in M500c bins and whether radii are already scaled by the true R500c. If so, b_HSE at r = R500c(true) is well defined. If not, report only M_HSE(z_high)/M_HSE(z_low), as already planned. Also record whether CTP is mass-weighted, emission-weighted or spectroscopic. The bias differs by that choice, and FLAMINGO and X-COP use spectroscopic-like temperatures.; Check that 0.5, 1 and 2 R500c lie inside the emulator's radial range and grid. If 2 R500c is outside, say so rather than extrapolating. Differencing the upper and lower band edges does not give a valid slope uncertainty, because band edges are not correlated realisations. Label it a crude bound, or difference adjacent bins and report the spread. No tool computes derivatives, so show every input value and every step of the arithmetic so a reader can verify it..

**Blocked — Test the mass dependence of the profile-slope-driven HSE bias, groups versus clusters, at both redshifts. This lets the FLAMINGO result (2409.07849) of groups rising and clusters falling with z be compared directly..** (The HACC CGD/CTP/CPP emulators have no halo-mass parameter or mass bins. Each prediction is one profile for an undocumented mass selection, so separate group-scale (1e13.5 Msun) and cluster-scale (1e14.5-15 Msun) profiles cannot be produced. Redshift coverage for these profiles also stops at z = 0.4987. Unblocking needs either documentation of the mass selection behind the profiles (q-06) or a different emulator or dataset that resolves mass.) I could not test mass dependence because the emulator has no mass input. list_observables (tc-261020_1-w1-d-04-20) and describe_parameters (tc-261020_1-w1-d-04-21) show that CGD, CTP and CPP take only redshift and 7 parameters: kappa_w, e_w, M_seed, v_kin, epsilon_kin, omega_m and sigma_8. One test prediction (CGD at z=0 with fiducial mid-range parameters; file /Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-combo-cluster-profiles/runs/261020_143128/CGD_z0.0000_prediction.csv, tc-261020_1-w1-d-04-25 and -27) returned a single 19-bin profile of rho_gas/rho_crit against r/R500c from 0.0154 to 2.74. The file has no mass column or mass bins. The cluster-profile emulators are also trained only for z = 0 to 0.4987, so a z of about 1 comparison is not possible either. From that test profile alone, the z=0 density log-slope near R500c, taken by finite difference between r/R500c = 0.866 (35.08) and 1.155 (16.86), is ln(16.862/35.076)/ln(1.1548/0.8660) = -0.7325/0.2878, about -2.55. This is one radius at one redshift for a single unknown mass, so it says nothing about mass dependence. I made no group or cluster predictions, slope sums or overlay plot, and I made no comparison with FLAMINGO. Dead end x-01 and question q-06 are posted.

**Finding:** FLAMINGO (Braspenning et al. 2024, arXiv:2409.07849): fiducial median b_HSE = (M_HSE,500c - M500c)/M500c goes from about -0.1 (groups) to about -0.2 (clusters). Scatter at fixed true mass is smallest, sigma(b) about 0.1, at M500c ~ 1e14 Msun. At fixed true mass, HSE masses rise with z for groups and fall with z for clusters, and the scatter grows. Models with lower gas fractions give more-biased group masses and less-biased cluster masses. The bias does not depend on the fitting function, but it does depend on fit quality: poorer fits give a stronger bias. The scatter comes from differences in pressure gradient, not from T(R500c).

**Finding:** X-COP (Eckert et al. 2018, arXiv:1805.00034), 13 nearby clusters with XMM+Planck: median non-thermal pressure fraction ~6% at R500 and ~10% at R200. This is lower than hydrodynamical simulations predict. With the Planck mass calibration, the gas fractions imply 1-b = 0.85 +/- 0.05 for SZ masses, with some evidence for a mass-dependent bias.

**Finding:** Nelson, Lau & Nagai 2014 (arXiv:1404.4636): the non-thermal pressure fraction profile is universal across redshift when radii are scaled to the mean matter density (R200m), not to the critical density. It depends strongly on mass accretion rate, and the non-thermal pressure is mainly radial. A fitting formula for f_nth(r/R200m) is given; parameter values are not yet extracted.

**Finding:** Simba (Sorini et al. 2024, arXiv:2409.05815), six feedback variants, 1e11 < M200c < 1e14 Msun, 0 < z < 4: gas-density profiles follow a power law. At fixed halo mass, slope and amplitude depend only weakly on redshift. With AGN jets on, haloes above M200c ~ 1e13 Msun have shallower (gentler) density profiles. A universal fitting formula for slope(M, z) and amplitude(M, z) is provided.

**Finding:** HACC emulator at design-midpoint parameters (kappa_w=3, e_w=0.6, M_seed=1.3, v_kin=0.65, eps_kin=0.61, omega_m=0.1375, sigma_8=0.8). Profiles are only available for z<=0.4987, so the pair used is z=0 and z=0.4987. CGD is rho_gas/rho_crit(z) and CTP is T/T500, on 19 log bins (0.015-2.74 R500c). Centred log-slopes, with 1-sigma errors from the GP std assuming independent bins. At z=0: s_n = -1.86+-0.10, -2.55+-0.16, -3.13+-0.07 and s_T = -0.27+-0.03, -0.58+-0.06, -1.12+-0.05 at 0.49, 1.0 and 2.05 R500c. At z=0.4987: s_n = -1.87+-0.10, -2.74+-0.10, -2.93+-0.06 and s_T = -0.35+-0.06, -0.50+-0.14, -1.54+-0.11. T(R500)/T500 is 0.592 at z=0 and 0.518 at z=0.4987. Assuming kT500 = G mu m_p M500/(2 R500), M_HSE(R500)/M500 = -(T/T500)(s_n+s_T)/2. This gives 0.925+-0.05 (b_HSE = 0.075) at z=0 and 0.840+-0.045 (b_HSE = 0.16) at z=0.4987, a ratio of 0.91.

**Finding:** Barranco-Llorca et al. 2025 (arXiv:2511.10730), AMR cluster mergers at 0 <= z <= 1.5: at z=0 the HSE bias correlates only mildly with dynamical state. During a major merger the bias dips sharply negative around the merger time, then shows a transient positive peak, then slowly returns to its pre-merger level. This is driven mainly by changes in the gas-density morphology and dynamics, not by thermodynamics, and it shows weak dependence on mass ratio and impact parameter.

**Finding:** Comparison overlays of the HACC emulator profiles at z=0 and z=0.4987 (midpoint parameters). In CGD (rho_gas/rho_crit(z)) the two redshifts agree within about 3% over 0.2-0.9 R500c. At z=0.4987 the density is about 6% lower at 1.15 R500c and about 13-14% lower at 1.5-2.05 R500c, then converges again at 2.74 R500c, and the core (r<0.1 R500c) is about 15-50% lower. In CTP (T/T500), z=0.4987 sits 7-13% below z=0 from 0.15 R500c to 1.15 R500c (12% lower at R500c itself), and the gap widens to 30% by 2.74 R500c.

- z=0: s_n = -1.86+-0.10, -2.55+-0.16, -3.13+-0.07; s_T = -0.27+-0.03, -0.58+-0.06, -1.12+-0.05.

Hydrostatic mass: I assumed mu=0.59 and the convention kT500 = G mu m_p M500/(2 R500), which gives M_HSE(R500)/M500 = -(T/T500)(s_n+s_T)/2. This gives 0.925+-0.05 (b_HSE about 0.075) at z=0 and 0.840+-0.045 (b_HSE about 0.16) at z=0.4987, a ratio of 0.91. The larger bias at z=0.4987 comes mainly from the 12% lower temperature at R500, not from a change in slopes. The absolute b_HSE values depend on the T500 convention; the ratio between redshifts is the more reliable number.

**Critic, wave 1** — continue: 6 findings stand up to the evidence, 1 questioned ('HACC emulator at design-midpoint parameters (kappa_w=3, e_w=0.6, M_seed=1.3, v_kin=0.65, e': The CSV excerpts quoted as evidence (tc-35/37/38/39) show only the first six innermost bins (r < 0.09 R500c). The arithmetic is internally consistent: 0.592*3.13/2 = 0.926, 0.518*3.24/2 = 0.839, and the stated errors follow from the slope errors. The interpretive part is not supported, however. **Finding:** Using eps_kin (kinetic AGN feedback efficiency, range 0.02-1.2) as the feedback lever, with the other parameters at the design midpoint (kappa_w=3, e_w=0.6, M_seed=1.3, v_kin=0.65, omega_m=0.1375, sigma_8=0.8), the HACC emulator produced CGD and CTP profiles at z=0 and z=0.4987 for eps_kin=0.02 and 1.2. They are plotted against the d-01 midpoint (eps_kin=0.61, z=0) in Figure 21 (CGD) and Figure 22 (CTP). The numerical slopes s_n+s_T at R500c have NOT yet been extracted from these files.

**Finding:** Nelson, Lau & Nagai 2014 (arXiv:1404.4636, Eq. 7, cited verbatim in references.bib) fit P_rand/P_tot(r) = 1 - A{1+exp[-((r/R200m)/B)^gamma]} with A=0.452+-0.001, B=0.841+-0.008, gamma=1.628+-0.019, valid to about 10% over 0.1-1.5 R200m out to z=1.5 (non-radiative ART runs, mass-weighted T and sigma). Evaluated at R500c: x = r/R200m = 0.5, 0.55 and 0.6 gives f_nth = 0.254, 0.274 and 0.294, with 1/(1-f_nth) = 1.34, 1.38 and 1.42. Assumption, computed by hand not with a tool: R500c is about 0.5-0.6 R200m, nearer 0.5 at z=0 and nearer 0.55-0.6 at z=0.5 because Omega_m(z) is higher. Because the profile is redshift-universal in r/R200m, the z dependence enters only through this radius conversion.

**Finding (preliminary):** Applying the Nelson et al. f_nth at R500c (0.25-0.29) as a multiplicative factor 1/(1-f_nth) = 1.34-1.42 to the emulator values M_HSE/M500 = 0.925 (z=0) and 0.840 (z=0.4987) from f-005 gives 1.24-1.31 at z=0 and 1.16-1.19 at z=0.4987. That is a 16-31% overcorrection. To reconcile the emulator directly, f_nth would need to be only about 0.075 (z=0) and 0.16 (z=0.4987). These values are closer to the X-COP estimate (about 6% at R500, f-002) than to the non-radiative Nelson fit. So either the emulator's T500 convention or its temperature weighting already absorbs part of the bias, or the HACC profiles carry less non-thermal pressure than the ART non-radiative runs.

**Finding:** FLAMINGO (arXiv:2409.07849) full text, Sec. 3.2-3.4 and Figs. 1, 2, 3 and 5:
- For 1e13.75 < M500c < 1e14.25 Msun, all five profile methods converge to a median b_HSE of about -0.1.
- The FLAMINGO calibration assumed a constant b of -0.257, taken from weak lensing, which agrees with the predictions for the most massive clusters.
- Fig. 2: volume-weighted profiles give a significantly smaller and less mass-dependent bias than X-ray-weighted ones, and mass-weighted profiles fall in between. The authors conclude that for M500c >> 1e13 Msun most of the bias comes from X-rays being a biased tracer of the gas.
- Fig. 5 (bias vs redshift, z = 0-1.5): as a function of true mass, the bias curves steepen with increasing redshift, while at fixed M_HSE they are almost unchanged except at z=1.5.
- Scatter grows to sigma about 0.35 at 5e14 Msun for fgas+2sigma.

Title: Hydrostatic mass bias for galaxy groups and clusters in the FLAMINGO simulations
Authors: Joey Braspenning, Joop Schaye, Matthieu Schaller, Roi Kugel, Scott T. Kay
Year: 2024
Abstract: The masses of galaxy clusters are commonly measured from X-ray observations under the assumption of hydrostatic equilibrium (HSE). This technique is known to underestimate the true mass systematically. The fiducial FLAMINGO cosmological hydrodynamical simulation predicts the median hydrostatic mass bias to increase from $b_\text{HSE} \equiv (M_\text{HSE,500c}-M_\text{500c})/M_\text{500c} \approx -0.1$ to -0.2 when the true mass increases from group to cluster mass scales. However, the bias is nearly independent of the hydrostatic mass. The scatter at fixed true mass is minimum for $M_\text{500c}\sim 10^{14}~\text{M}_\odot$, where $σ(b_\text{HSE})\approx 0.1$, but increases rapidly towards lower and higher masses. At a fixed true mass, the hydrostatic masses increase (decrease) with redshift on group (cluster) scales, and the scatter increases. The bias is insensitive to the choice of analytic functions assumed to represent the density and temperature profiles, but it is sensitive to the goodness of fit, with poorer fits corresponding to a stronger median bias and a larger scatter. The bias is also sensitive to the strength of stellar and AGN feedback. Models predicting lower gas fractions yield more (less) biased masses for groups (clusters). The scatter in the bias at fixed true mass is due to differences in the pressure gradients rather than in the temperature at $R_\text{500c}$. The total kinetic energies within $r_\text{500c}$ in low- and high-mass clusters are sub- and super-virial, respectively, though all become sub-virial when external pressure is accounted for. Analyses of the terms in the virial and Euler equations suggest that non-thermal motions, including rotation, account for most of the hydrostatic mass bias. However, we find that the mass bias estimated from X-ray luminosity weighted profiles strongly overestimates the deviations from hydrostatic equilibrium.

Title: The signature of major mergers on the hydrostatic mass bias of galaxy clusters
Authors: Isac Barranco-Llorca, David Vallés-Pérez, Susana Planelles, Vicent Quilis
Year: 2025
Abstract: While galaxy cluster masses are fundamental cosmological observables, estimates based on intra-cluster medium observations rely on hydrostatic equilibrium, introducing a systematic bias. We investigate how mergers drive the time evolution of this hydrostatic mass bias, identifying the dominant physical mechanisms and their dependence on dynamical state and merger history. Using a high-resolution AMR Eulerian+$N$-body cosmological simulation, we analyse a sample of cluster mergers within $1.5 \leq z \leq 0$, comparing true and hydrostatic masses derived from gas density and temperature profiles, and tracing their evolution. At $z=0$, the hydrostatic mass bias shows a mild correlation with dynamical state. During major mergers, the bias follows a characteristic trend: a sharp negative dip around the merger time, a transient positive peak, and a gradual return to pre-merger levels. This behaviour is primarily driven by morphological and dynamical reconfigurations of the gas density within the ICM, while thermodynamical processes play a secondary role. The pattern shows no strong dependence on secondary parameters, such as mass ratio or impact parameter, but it can be fitted to a simple time-dependent functional form. This trend is present at radii $r\le R_{\mathrm{vir}}$, although with reduced amplitude and shorter timescales as the radius decreases. Hydrostatic mass bias is closely linked, albeit in a non-trivial way, with the merging history of galaxy clusters. We find that the bias values are weakly correlated with the dynamical state of clusters. Nevertheless, our results give a robust estimation of the hydrostatic mass bias values in the pre-merger, merging, and post-merger phases. These findings highlight the importance of delving deeper into the observational assessment of cluster assembly state in order to improve mass estimations for cosmological analyses.

5. SUMMARY AND DISCUSSION
In this work we presented the redshift and mass inde-
pendent non-thermal pressure fraction proﬁle using a mass-
limited, cosmologically representative sample of 65 massive
galaxy clusters from a high resolution hydrodynamical cos-
mological simulation. This result is relevant in accounting for
the systematic effects of non-thermal pressure on X-ray and
microwave measurements of galaxy clusters and cosmologi-
cal inferences based on these measurements.
We found that the mean non-thermal pressure fraction pro-
ﬁle exhibits remarkable universality in redshift and mass
when we deﬁne the size of cluster halos using the mean matter
density of the universe, instead of the critical density. How-
ever, we also showed that there is strong dependence in the
non-thermal pressure fraction proﬁle on the halo’s mass ac-
cretion rate: clusters that are rapidly accreting have an overall
higher non-thermal pressure fraction. As such, the mass ac-
cretion rate is a major source of systematic scatter in the mean
non-thermal pressure fraction proﬁle.
A robust and quantitative proxy for measuring mass accre-
tion rate is therefore needed to account for this effect, es-
pecially with the upcoming multi-wavelength cluster surveys
where statistical errors will be considerably smaller than sys-
tematic uncertainties arising from our ignorance of cluster as-
trophysics. We note that the current method of characterizing
the mass accretion rate using the fractional mass increase be-
tween z = 0 and z = 0.5 is by no means unique, and can only
be applied to z = 0 clusters. Future work should focus on de-
veloping quantitative measures of the mass accretion rate of
halos that can be applied to halos across a wide range of red-
shifts, and relate these measures to observable proxies of the
dynamical states of clusters.
We found no systematic mass dependence in the univer-
sal non-thermal pressure fraction proﬁle. But given that our
sample contains only massive clusters, the independence in
mass should be checked with sample of lower mass halos.
Since slowly accreting halos have smaller non-thermal pres-
sure fraction, we expect that lower mass groups and galaxies,
which should experience less physical mass accretion than
high mass clusters, to have lower non-thermal pressure frac-
tion proﬁle. However, we note that smaller mass halos are
more susceptible to non-gravitational physics (such as gas
cooling and energy injections from stars and active galactic
nuclei) which can inﬂuence the net accretion rate into and
within the halos in a non-trivial way.
We found that the gas velocity is predominantly radial, with
the velocity anisotropy parameter increasing from ≈ 0.1 to
≈ 0.6 from 0.2r200m to r200m. Moreover, we found that the
velocity anisotropy proﬁle is also universal across redshift
when halos are deﬁned using the mean matter density, indi-
cating that gas velocity anisotropy is also a self-similar quan-
tity. This result can be useful since the velocity anisotropy
cannot be easily measured in observations, as we can only
measure line-of-sight velocities from Doppler width measure-
ments, e.g., with the upcoming ASTRO-H in the near future.
Measurements of gas motions tangential to the line-of-sight
are possible with resonant scattering but difﬁcult (e.g., Zhu-
ravleva et al. 2011).
We provided ﬁtting formulae for the universal non-thermal
pressure fraction and gas velocity anisotropy proﬁles that
work remarkably well within r200m and out to redshift z = 1.5.
One application of our ﬁtting formulas is the recovery of to-
tal mass of relaxed clusters by accounting for the hydrostatic
mass bias. The effect of velocity anisotropy should be in-
cluded in the mass recovery, since the formalism for the full

# Hydrostatic mass bias and profile-shape evolution: a literature baseline and HACC-emulator test at z = 0 and z = 0.4987

## Abstract

This report combines a survey of hydrostatic-equilibrium (HSE) mass bias in galaxy clusters with a test using a HACC-based hydrodynamics emulator. The emulator was used to predict gas-density (CGD) and temperature (CTP) profiles at the midpoint of its design space, at z = 0 and z = 0.4987.

The pairing differs from the intended z = 0 vs z = 1 because the cluster-profile emulators stop at z = 0.4987. The log-slopes of the profiles at R500c barely change between the two redshifts:

- s_n + s_T = -3.13 at z = 0.
- s_n + s_T = -3.24 at z = 0.4987.

The main change is in the temperature normalisation, with T(R500)/T500 falling from 0.592 to 0.518. Under an assumed T500 convention this gives:

- M_HSE/M500 = 0.925 ± 0.051 at z = 0 and 0.840 ± 0.048 at z = 0.4987.
- In the FLAMINGO sign convention, b = -0.075 and -0.160, so Δb = -0.085 ± 0.070.

The bias becomes more negative with redshift, as FLAMINGO finds for clusters. The trend is only about 1.2σ, both from the density-plus-temperature route and from the emulator's own pressure profile.

The pressure profile agrees with the density and temperature slopes at R500 but is far shallower at 2 R500. This indicates that the three emulated profiles are not mutually consistent at large radius.

Three further limits apply:

- A feedback-robustness test was run but not reduced to numbers.
- The emulator exposes no halo mass, so the FLAMINGO group-versus-cluster comparison could not be done.
- The absolute bias values depend on an undocumented T500 and temperature-weighting convention.

## Background

**Bias magnitude in simulations.** Hydrodynamical simulations consistently find that HSE masses from X-ray and SZ data underestimate the true mass. The FLAMINGO study (arXiv:2409.07849) defines b_HSE = (M_HSE,500c - M500c)/M500c and reports the following:

- The median bias goes from about -0.1 for groups to about -0.2 for clusters.
- The scatter is smallest near M500c ~ 10^14 Msun, with σ(b) ≈ 0.1. It grows to about 0.35 at 5×10^14 Msun in the fgas+2σ variant.
- At fixed true mass, HSE masses rise with redshift for groups and fall with redshift for clusters, and the scatter grows with z.
- Feedback models with lower gas fractions give more-biased group masses and less-biased cluster masses.
- The bias does not depend on which fitting function is used, but poorer fits give a stronger bias.
- The scatter comes from differences in the pressure gradient, not from T(R500c).

From the FLAMINGO full text:

- In the 10^13.75–10^14.25 Msun bin, all five profile methods converge to b ≈ -0.1.
- The FLAMINGO calibration assumed a constant b = -0.257.
- Volume-weighted profiles give a much smaller and less mass-dependent bias than X-ray-weighted ones, with mass-weighted profiles in between. The authors attribute most of the bias at M500c ≫ 10^13 Msun to X-rays being a biased tracer of the gas.
- As a function of true mass, b(M) steepens with redshift over z = 0–1.5. At fixed M_HSE it is nearly unchanged except at z = 1.5.

**Non-thermal pressure.** Nelson, Lau & Nagai (arXiv:1404.4636) give a fit to the non-thermal pressure fraction:

f_nth = 1 - A{1 + exp[-((r/R200m)/B)^γ]}, with A = 0.452 ± 0.001, B = 0.841 ± 0.008 and γ = 1.628 ± 0.019.

The fit comes from non-radiative ART runs using mass-weighted T and σ. It is accurate to about 10% over 0.1–1.5 R200m out to z = 1.5, and it is universal in redshift when radii are scaled to R200m. The fraction depends strongly on the mass accretion rate.

**Observations.** The X-COP sample (arXiv:1805.00034) of 13 nearby clusters gives:

- A median non-thermal fraction of about 6% at R500 and about 10% at R200, lower than simulations predict.
- 1 - b = 0.85 ± 0.05 with the Planck calibration, with some evidence for a mass-dependent bias.

**Gas-density slopes.** Simba (arXiv:2409.05815) finds that gas-density profiles follow power laws whose slope and amplitude depend only weakly on redshift at fixed mass over 0 < z < 4. AGN jets flatten the profiles above M200c ~ 10^13 Msun. This suggests that any redshift evolution of the bias should come from the temperature rather than the density slope.

**Mergers.** A recent merger study (arXiv:2511.10730, abstract only) finds that the bias dips sharply negative during a major merger, then peaks briefly positive, then relaxes back. This is driven mainly by changes in the gas-density structure rather than by thermodynamics.

**Relevance to this test.** The HSE mass depends on the log-slopes d ln n/d ln r and d ln T/d ln r and on T itself, not on the density amplitude. Profile-shape evolution therefore enters the bias directly.

Other papers identified but not read in detail are:

- arXiv:1112.3659 (merger-driven bias evolution).
- arXiv:1306.3993 and arXiv:1308.6589 (methods for computing the bias, and its origin).
- arXiv:1507.04338 (Shi–Komatsu analytic non-thermal model).
- arXiv:1608.04388 (mass-modelling framework).
- arXiv:1805.00035, arXiv:1805.00042 and arXiv:2112.07554 (X-COP mass and universal profiles, and non-thermal tracing).
- arXiv:2010.00619 (CAMELS). Note that the emulator used here is HACC-based, not CAMELS-based.

## Results

### Emulator set-up

The emulator's CGD, CTP and CPP (pressure) profiles take seven inputs plus redshift. The inputs, set to the midpoints of their design ranges, are:

| Parameter | Description | Midpoint used |
|---|---|---|
| kappa_w | AGN wind coupling | 3 |
| e_w | AGN wind energy fraction | 0.6 |
| M_seed | Black-hole seed mass | 1.3 |
| v_kin | Kinetic feedback parameter | 0.65 |
| eps_kin | Kinetic AGN feedback efficiency | 0.61 |
| omega_m | Matter density | 0.1375 |
| sigma_8 | Power-spectrum normalisation | 0.8 |

There is no fiducial parameter set, so the midpoints were used. The profiles have these properties:

- They are already self-similarly scaled: CGD is ρ_gas/ρ_crit(z), CTP is T/T500 and CPP is P/P500.
- Each covers 19 logarithmic bins from 0.0154 to 2.74 R500c, so 2 R500c lies inside the grid.
- Each profile is for a single, undocumented halo selection. There is no mass column and no true M500c.
- The cluster profiles cover only z ≤ 0.4987.

### Profile shape change between z = 0 and z = 0.4987

[[FIGURE 9]]

Figure 9 overlays CGD at the two redshifts. The density at z = 0.4987 behaves as follows relative to z = 0:

- It agrees within about 3% over 0.2–0.9 R500c.
- It is about 6% lower at 1.15 R500c and 13–14% lower at 1.5–2.05 R500c.
- It converges again at 2.74 R500c.

The core (r < 0.1 R500c) appears 15–50% lower at z = 0.4987. The emulator uncertainty there is very large: the innermost bin is 1018 ± 689 at z = 0.4987 against 2154 ± 258 at z = 0. The core difference should therefore be treated as not significant.

[[FIGURE 10]]

Figure 10 overlays CTP. Relative to z = 0, the temperature at z = 0.4987 is:

- 7–13% lower over 0.15–1.15 R500c.
- 12% lower at R500c itself.
- About 30% lower at 2.74 R500c.

### Log-slopes and the HSE mass ratio

Slopes are centred finite differences in ln r over neighbouring bins centred at 0.49, 1.00 and 2.05 R500c. The errors come from the emulator's Gaussian-process standard deviation, assuming independent bins.

| Radius (R500c) | s_n (z=0) | s_n (z=0.4987) | s_T (z=0) | s_T (z=0.4987) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.49 | -1.86 ± 0.10 | -1.87 ± 0.10 | -0.27 ± 0.03 | -0.35 ± 0.06 |
| 1.00 | -2.55 ± 0.16 | -2.74 ± 0.10 | -0.58 ± 0.06 | -0.50 ± 0.14 |
| 2.05 | -3.13 ± 0.07 | -2.93 ± 0.06 | -1.12 ± 0.05 | -1.54 ± 0.11 |

As a check, the z = 0 density slope near R500c follows directly from the CSV values. Between r/R500c = 0.866 (35.08) and 1.155 (16.86), ln(16.862/35.076)/ln(1.1548/0.8660) ≈ -2.55.

At R500c the slopes barely change with redshift:

- s_n + s_T = -3.13 ± 0.17 at z = 0 and -3.24 ± 0.17 at z = 0.4987, consistent within errors.
- The density slope does not evolve significantly at any of the three radii, in line with the Simba expectation.
- The clearest shape change is the steepening of the temperature slope at 2 R500c, nominally about 3.6σ. This rests on finite differences of emulator means with independent errors and has not been checked against a smooth fit.

**Mass ratio.** T(R500)/T500 was taken as the geometric mean of the 0.866 and 1.155 R500c bins, giving 0.5916 ± 0.0047 at z = 0 and 0.5181 ± 0.0101 at z = 0.4987. The HSE mass ratio uses μ = 0.59 and the convention kT500 = G μ m_p M500/(2 R500), so that M_HSE(R500)/M500 = -(T/T500)(s_n + s_T)/2. This gives:

| Quantity | z = 0 | z = 0.4987 |
|---|---|---|
| M_HSE/M500 | 0.925 ± 0.051 | 0.840 ± 0.048 |
| b (FLAMINGO convention) | -0.075 ± 0.051 | -0.160 ± 0.048 |

The ratio between redshifts is 0.91. Because the slope sum barely changes, the larger bias at z = 0.4987 comes mainly from the 12% lower temperature at R500, not from profile shape. The absolute b values depend on the assumed T500 convention. The critic flagged two problems with this result: the significance had to be tested, and the sign convention initially differed from FLAMINGO's. Both are addressed in the next subsection.

### Pressure-profile cross-check and significance

The emulator's own pressure profile gives an independent slope s_P, compared here with s_n + s_T over the same bin pairs.

| Radius | z | s_P (CPP) | s_n + s_T | Difference |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.49 R500 | 0 | -1.981 ± 0.042 | -2.133 ± 0.104 | 1.3σ |
| 0.49 R500 | 0.4987 | -1.874 ± 0.088 | -2.218 ± 0.117 | 2.4σ |
| 1.00 R500 | 0 | -3.052 ± 0.113 | -3.128 ± 0.171 | 0.37σ |
| 1.00 R500 | 0.4987 | -3.232 ± 0.154 | -3.243 ± 0.172 | 0.05σ |
| 2.05 R500 | 0 | -2.877 ± 0.042 | -4.249 ± 0.086 | 14.4σ |
| 2.05 R500 | 0.4987 | -1.815 ± 0.207 | -4.463 ± 0.125 | 10.9σ |

The routes agree at R500, so the R500 mass estimate is robust to which route is used. Beyond R500 the pressure profile is not the product of the density and temperature profiles.

With the T(R500)/T500 error propagated, the two routes give:

| Slope used | z=0 M_HSE/M500 | z=0.4987 M_HSE/M500 | Difference | Δb (FLAMINGO convention) | Significance |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| s_n + s_T | 0.925 ± 0.051 | 0.840 ± 0.048 | 0.085 ± 0.070 | -0.085 ± 0.070 | 1.2σ |
| s_P (CPP) | 0.903 ± 0.034 | 0.837 ± 0.043 | 0.066 ± 0.055 | -0.066 ± 0.055 | 1.2σ |

From the pressure route, b = -0.097 ± 0.034 at z = 0 and -0.163 ± 0.043 at z = 0.4987. Both routes give a bias that becomes more negative with redshift, the same direction as FLAMINGO for clusters, but neither is statistically significant.

The quoted errors treat bins and redshifts as independent. Correlated emulator errors could move the significance in either direction.

### Feedback sensitivity (incomplete)

The feedback test used kinetic AGN efficiency eps_kin, varied to the ends of its range (0.02 and 1.2) with the other parameters held at their midpoints. Choosing eps_kin was a judgement call, because the emulator does not indicate which parameter controls the slopes. CGD and CTP were predicted at both redshifts for both values.

[[FIGURE 21]]

[[FIGURE 22]]

Figures 21 (CGD) and 22 (CTP) each overlay five profiles: the midpoint (eps_kin = 0.61) at z = 0, and eps_kin = 0.02 and 1.2 at both redshifts. The slopes, T/T500 and M_HSE/M500 for these runs were not extracted. It therefore cannot yet be said whether feedback moves the bias more or less than the redshift change does. The fGas observable was not run.

### Non-thermal correction

The Nelson et al. fit was evaluated at R500c assuming R500c ≈ 0.5–0.6 R200m (about 0.5 at z = 0 and 0.55–0.6 at z = 0.5). This conversion and the evaluation were done by hand, not with a tool. The results are:

| x = r/R200m | f_nth | Correction factor 1/(1 - f_nth) |
|---|---|---|
| 0.50 | 0.254 | 1.34 |
| 0.55 | 0.274 | 1.38 |
| 0.60 | 0.294 | 1.42 |

Applying these factors to the emulator ratios gives 1.24–1.31 at z = 0 and 1.16–1.19 at z = 0.4987, an overcorrection of 16–31%.

Reconciling the emulator directly would need f_nth ≈ 1 - M_HSE/M500 ≈ 0.075 at z = 0 and 0.16 at z = 0.4987. These are closer to the X-COP value of about 6% than to the non-radiative Nelson fit. This conclusion relies on the hand-derived R500c–R200m mapping and on the assumed T500 convention, so it is low confidence and has not been independently verified.

## Discussion

**Where profile shape matters.** Profile-shape evolution between z = 0 and z ≈ 0.5 has little effect on the HSE mass reconstruction at R500c:

- The density slope is stable, as Simba (arXiv:2409.05815) predicts.
- The total slope changes by only about 0.1.
- The apparent increase in bias with redshift is carried by the temperature normalisation, T(R500)/T500.

Shape evolution does matter at 2 R500c, where the temperature slope steepens. At that radius, however, the emulated pressure profile disagrees with density times temperature by more than 10σ. Any outskirts mass reconstruction from these emulators is therefore currently unreliable. Possible causes include:

- ⟨P⟩ ≠ ⟨ρ⟩⟨T⟩ under halo-to-halo scatter or clumping.
- Different halo samples or weightings behind each emulator.
- Edge effects near the 2.74 R500c grid boundary.

The flattening of the pressure slope with redshift at 2.05 R500c, from -2.88 to -1.82, deserves caution for the same reasons.

**Comparison with FLAMINGO.** The direction of Δb matches FLAMINGO's cluster-scale trend (arXiv:2409.07849). The magnitude cannot be compared quantitatively, for three reasons:

- The halo mass behind the emulated profiles is unknown.
- The temperature weighting (mass-weighted or spectroscopic-like) is undocumented.
- The subgrid models in HACC, FLAMINGO and Simba differ.

FLAMINGO's weighting result offers one possible reconciliation. If CTP is mass-weighted, FLAMINGO would predict a bias smaller in magnitude than -0.2, compatible with the emulator's -0.075 to -0.16.

**Possible confounds.** Two effects could mimic or distort the redshift trend:

- **Selection.** If the emulator's stack uses a fixed mass threshold, the mean mass is lower at z = 0.4987, and part of the trend could be a selection effect.
- **Normalisation.** The critic noted that T(R500)/T500 ≈ 0.59 is low compared with observed universal profiles, which the critic put at roughly 0.8–0.9 at R500 for X-COP. This hints that the emulator's T500 normalisation differs from the assumed convention, which would shift every absolute b.

**Non-thermal pressure.** The non-radiative Nelson et al. fraction overcorrects the emulator masses. The implied required fraction is closer to the X-COP observation (arXiv:1805.00034). Possible explanations are:

- The emulator's convention or weighting already absorbs part of the bias.
- HACC haloes carry less non-thermal support than non-radiative ART runs.

These cannot be distinguished without the emulator documentation.

**Dead ends.**

- **Group versus cluster mass dependence.** The emulator has no mass input and returns one profile per call, so group-scale and cluster-scale profiles could not be produced. The z ≈ 1 comparison was also impossible.
- **Documentation search and X-COP benchmark.** The search for HACC mass-selection and temperature-weighting documentation, and the X-COP universal-profile slope benchmark (arXiv:1805.00042), were not attempted because the tool budget ran out. They are not intrinsically blocked.

## Limitations

**What the emulator does not provide.**

- There is no true M500c and no mass selection, so absolute biases rest on an assumed kT500 convention. Only the redshift ratio (0.91) is relatively convention-independent.
- The temperature weighting is unknown. This matters because FLAMINGO shows the bias depends strongly on weighting.
- Redshift coverage stops at z = 0.4987, so z = 1 was not tested.

**How slopes and errors were computed.**

- Slopes are finite differences of emulator means with independent-bin errors.
- No smooth-function fit (for example a Vikhlinin-type model) was tried.
- Correlated emulator errors were not modelled.
- The 3.6σ temperature-slope change and the 1.2σ bias change are therefore uncertain in significance.

**Incomplete analyses.** The feedback runs exist but were not analysed, and fGas was never predicted. No plots with uncertainty bands were made for individual predictions.

**Literature coverage.**

- The baseline rests on four papers recorded with verbatim quotes, short of the six targeted.
- The FLAMINGO numbers taken from the full text were not recorded with quotes, and its per-mass-bin b(z) values are only plotted, not tabulated.
- The merger result is from the abstract only.
- arXiv:1805.00035, arXiv:1805.00042, arXiv:1507.04338 and the Simba fit coefficients were not extracted.

**Non-thermal correction.** The R500c-to-R200m conversion used for it was assumed and computed by hand.

## Open directions

1. Extract s_n + s_T, T/T500 and M_HSE/M500 at R500c from the existing eps_kin = 0.02 and 1.2 profiles to test whether the feedback-induced shift exceeds the 0.085 redshift change.
2. Search for HACC profile documentation (halo-mass selection, T500 definition, temperature weighting) to turn the relative bias into an absolute one and to test the selection explanation.
3. Diagnose why the emulated pressure profile is much shallower than density times temperature beyond R500, and decide which is the correct input for outskirts HSE masses.
4. Refit the profiles with smooth analytic models and propagate correlated emulator errors to re-assess the significance of the temperature-slope steep

result.summary:
The redshift change in M_HSE/M500 is not statistically robust: it is about 1.2 sigma whichever way the slope is computed. I predicted CPP (P/P500) at the d-01 midpoint parameters (tc-...-62, -63). The files are CPP_z0.0000_prediction.csv and CPP_z0.4987_prediction.csv in /Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-combo-cluster-profiles/runs/261020_143128/. The CGD, CTP and CPP bin values were read verbatim from the CSVs (tc-...-64 to -67, -69, -70). Slopes are centred finite differences over the same bin pairs as d-01 (0.365/0.649, 0.866/1.155 and 1.540/2.738 R500c), with GP errors treated as independent.

**Pressure-slope cross-check (f-012).** s_P from CPP compared with s_n+s_T from CGD and CTP:
- 0.49 R500, z=0: -1.981+-0.042 vs -2.133+-0.104, a 1.3 sigma difference.
- 0.49 R500, z=0.4987: -1.874+-0.088 vs -2.218+-0.117, 2.4 sigma.
- 1.00 R500, z=0: -3.052+-0.113 vs -3.128+-0.171, 0.37 sigma.
- 1.00 R500, z=0.4987: -3.232+-0.154 vs -3.243+-0.172, 0.05 sigma.
- 2.05 R500, z=0: -2.877+-0.042 vs -4.249+-0.086, 14 sigma.
- 2.05 R500, z=0.4987: -1.815+-0.207 vs -4.463+-0.125, 11 sigma.

CPP agrees with the density and temperature profiles at R500 but is much shallower beyond it. So at large radius CPP is not CGD x CTP, which points to a different averaging, weighting or halo sample (q-09).

**Mass ratio and bias (f-013).** T(R500)/T500, taken as the geometric mean of the two bins either side of R500, is 0.5916+-0.0047 at z=0 and 0.5181+-0.0101 at z=0.4987. With that error propagated:

| Slope used | z=0 M_HSE/M500 | z=0.4987 M_HSE/M500 | Difference | Significance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| s_n+s_T | 0.925+-0.051 | 0.840+-0.048 | 0.085+-0.070 | 1.2 sigma |
| s_P (CPP) | 0.903+-0.034 | 0.837+-0.043 | 0.066+-0.055 | 1.2 sigma |

In the FLAMINGO convention, b = (M_HSE-M500)/M500:
- From s_n+s_T: b = -0.075+-0.051 at z=0 and -0.160+-0.048 at z=0.4987, so Delta b = -0.085+-0.070.
- From CPP: b = -0.097+-0.034 and -0.163+-0.043, so Delta b = -0.066+-0.055.

The bias becomes more negative with redshift, the same direction FLAMINGO finds for clusters, but the trend is not significant.

**Caveats:**
- The finite-difference errors assume the bins are independent; correlated GP errors would change them.
- The kT500 = G mu m_p M500/(2 R500) convention sets the absolute b values.
- The mass selection behind the profiles is undocumented (q-06). If it is a fixed mass threshold, part of the redshift trend could be a selection effect.

**Still open:** q-09, the origin of the CPP versus CGD x CTP mismatch beyond R500. No figures were made in this direction.

brief.summary: Simulations and observations agree that X-ray/SZ hydrostatic (HSE) masses come out too low. Simulations typically give b of about 0.1-0.2, mostly from non-thermal pressure (turbulence, bulk motions, rotation) and from mergers. FLAMINGO (2409.07849) finds the median bias grows from about -0.1 on group scales to about -0.2 on cluster scales. At fixed true mass, HSE masses rise with redshift for groups and fall for clusters, and the scatter grows with redshift. The bias also depends on feedback strength and on how well the density and temperature profiles are fitted. Merger studies (1112.3659, 2511.10730) show the bias changes over time, with transient spikes after major mergers. Earlier simulation work (1306.3993, 1308.6589, 1404.4636) finds the non-thermal pressure fraction rising with radius and redshift, because higher-z clusters are accreting faster. Observationally, X-COP clusters out to R200 (1805.00035, 1805.00034, 2112.07554) show low non-thermal support (about 6% at R500) and a small bias in relaxed systems. Profile shape matters because the HSE mass depends on the log-slopes d ln n_gas/d ln r and d ln T/d ln r, not on amplitudes. Simba shows feedback changes gas-density slopes as a function of mass and redshift (2409.05815), so slope evolution between redshifts feeds directly into how the bias evolves. Warning: none of my tools (search_arxiv, web_search, search_arxiv_abstracts, get_arxiv_metadata) is a hydrodynamics emulator, and my searches found no tool or paper using the names CGD/CTP, so I could not produce the requested profile predictions.

result.summary:
This direction is done except for one item: the separate plot_prediction figure with an uncertainty band for each observable was not made, because the tool budget ran out. The redshift pair is z=0 vs z=0.4987, not z=0 vs z=1, because the CGD and CTP profiles only go up to z=0.4987. The emulator has no fiducial parameter set, so I used the midpoint of every design range: kappa_w=3, e_w=0.6, M_seed=1.3, v_kin=0.65, eps_kin=0.61, omega_m=0.1375, sigma_8=0.8. The profiles are already self-similarly scaled: CGD is rho_gas/rho_crit(z) and CTP is T/T500, on 19 logarithmic bins from 0.015 to 2.74 R500c. So 2 R500c is inside the grid (this answers q-02), and step 7 needed no extra rescaling. The emulator does not give the halo-mass bin, a true M500c, the T500 definition, or whether T is mass-weighted or spectroscopic-like, so q-01 and q-03 stay open.

Prediction files (in /Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-combo-cluster-profiles/runs/261020_143128/): CGD_z0.0000_prediction.csv, CGD_z0.4987_prediction.csv, CTP_z0.0000_prediction.csv, CTP_z0.4987_prediction.csv.

Log-slopes are centred finite differences in ln r over neighbouring bins centred at 0.49, 1.00 and 2.05 R500c. The 1-sigma errors use the emulator's standard deviation and treat bins as independent.
- z=0: s_n = -1.86+-0.10, -2.55+-0.16, -3.13+-0.07; s_T = -0.27+-0.03, -0.58+-0.06, -1.12+-0.05.
- z=0.4987: s_n = -1.87+-0.10, -2.74+-0.10, -2.93+-0.06; s_T = -0.35+-0.06, -0.50+-0.14, -1.54+-0.11.

At R500 the total slope s_n+s_T is -3.13 at z=0 and -3.24 at z=0.4987, the same within the errors (about +-0.16 each). The clear shape change is the temperature slope at 2 R500, which steepens by about 3.6 sigma. T(R500)/T500 falls from 0.592 at z=0 to 0.518 at z=0.4987.

Hydrostatic mass: I assumed mu=0.59 and the convention kT500 = G mu m_p M500/(2 R500), which gives M_HSE(R500)/M500 = -(T/T500)(s_n+s_T)/2. This gives 0.925+-0.05 (b_HSE about 0.075) at z=0 and 0.840+-0.045 (b_HSE about 0.16) at z=0.4987, a ratio of 0.91. The larger bias at z=0.4987 comes mainly from the 12% lower temperature at R500, not from a change in slopes. The absolute b_HSE values depend on the T500 convention; the ratio between redshifts is the more reliable number.

Comparison plots: Figure 9 (CGD_comparison.png) and Figure 10 (CTP_comparison.png), same directory. Density at z=0.4987 agrees with z=0 within about 3% over 0.2-0.9 R500c and is 13-14% lower at 1.5-2.05 R500c. Temperature at z=0.4987 is 7-13% lower over 0.15-1.15 R500c and 30% lower at 2.74 R500c.

Findings posted: f-005 and f-007.

Established values, posted as findings:

(f-001, tc-40) FLAMINGO, 2409.07849:
- The median bias b_HSE = (M_HSE,500c - M500c)/M500c goes from about -0.1 for groups to about -0.2 for clusters.
- The scatter is smallest near M500c ~ 1e14 Msun, at sigma(b) about 0.1.
- At fixed true mass, HSE masses rise with redshift for groups and fall for clusters, and the scatter grows with redshift.
- Feedback models with lower gas fractions give more-biased group masses and less-biased cluster masses.
- The bias does not depend on which fitting function is used, but poorer fits give a stronger bias.
- The scatter comes from differences in the pressure gradient, not from the temperature at R500c.

(f-002, tc-41) X-COP, 1805.00034:
- The non-thermal pressure fraction is about 6% at R500 and about 10% at R200.
- With the Planck mass calibration, 1-b = 0.85 +/- 0.05.

(f-003, tc-42) Nelson, Lau and Nagai 2014, 1404.4636:
- The non-thermal pressure fraction profile is the same at all redshifts when radius is scaled to R200m (mean matter density), not to the critical density.
- It depends strongly on how fast the cluster is accreting mass.
- The fitted parameter values were not extracted.

(f-004, tc-43) Simba, 2409.05815:
- Gas-density profiles follow a power law. At fixed mass, the slope and amplitude depend only weakly on redshift (0 < z < 4).
- Turning on AGN jets makes the density profile shallower for M200c above about 1e13 Msun.
- Implication for d-01: changes in the bias with redshift should come mainly from the temperature slope and mass scaling, not from the density slope.

(f-006, tc-54) Merger study, 2511.10730: during a major merger the bias dips sharply negative, then peaks briefly positive, then slowly returns to its pre-merger level. This comes mainly from changes in the gas-density structure. This result is from the abstract only and was not added with cite.

findings.claim: FLAMINGO (Braspenning et al. 2024, arXiv:2409.07849): fiducial median b_HSE = (M_HSE,500c - M500c)/M500c goes from about -0.1 (groups) to about -0.2 (clusters). Scatter at fixed true mass is smallest, sigma(b) about 0.1, at M500c ~ 1e14 Msun. At fixed true mass, HSE masses rise with z for groups and fall with z for clusters, and the scatter grows. Models with lower gas fractions give more-biased group masses and less-biased cluster masses. The bias does not depend on the fitting function, but it does depend on fit quality: poorer fits give a stronger bias. The scatter comes from differences in pressure gradient, not from T(R500c).

findings.claim: X-COP (Eckert et al. 2018, arXiv:1805.00034), 13 nearby clusters with XMM+Planck: median non-thermal pressure fraction ~6% at R500 and ~10% at R200. This is lower than hydrodynamical simulations predict. With the Planck mass calibration, the gas fractions imply 1-b = 0.85 +/- 0.05 for SZ masses, with some evidence for a mass-dependent bias.

Nelson, Lau & Nagai 2014 (arXiv:1404.4636): the non-thermal pressure fraction profile is universal across redshift when radii are scaled to the mean matter density (R200m), not to the critical density. It depends strongly on mass accretion rate, and the non-thermal pressure is mainly radial. A fitting formula for f_nth(r/R200m) is given; parameter values are not yet extracted.

Simba (Sorini et al. 2024, arXiv:2409.05815), six feedback variants, 1e11 < M200c < 1e14 Msun, 0 < z < 4: gas-density profiles follow a power law. At fixed halo mass, slope and amplitude depend only weakly on redshift. With AGN jets on, haloes above M200c ~ 1e13 Msun have shallower (gentler) density profiles. A universal fitting formula for slope(M, z) and amplitude(M, z) is provided.

evidence.note: Implication for d-01: the weak z-dependence of slope at fixed mass means any bias evolution in the emulator should come mostly from the temperature slope and mass scaling, not from the density slope. The Simba mass range stops at 1e14.

questions.text: Are the CGD and CTP profiles given per halo-mass bin, and does the emulator provide a true M500c? If not, b_HSE can only be reported as a relative redshift change.
What radial range does the emulator cover? Is 2 R500c inside it, or must the slopes there be extrapolated?
Is CTP mass-weighted or spectroscopic-like temperature? The answer changes the expected HSE bias.
Is the emulator's uncertainty band large enough that finite-difference slopes are noise-dominated? If so, should we fit a smooth (e.g. Vikhlinin-type) function before differentiating?
No HPC run is planned. The emulator predictions are quick local calls, so set_dispatch is not needed unless the parameter grid grows substantially.

What halo-mass selection (M500c range or stack) defines the HACC CGD/CTP emulator profiles? The emulator metadata does not document it, and without it a group-versus-cluster comparison with FLAMINGO (2409.07849) cannot be made.

Still to extract: the numerical Nelson et al. 2014 f_nth(r/R200m) fit parameters (1404.4636 Sec. results), the FLAMINGO per-mass-bin b(z) values and figure number (2409.07849), the X-COP universal profile parameters (1805.00042), and the Simba slope-fit coefficients (2409.05815). The full texts are already downloaded in the run directory.

From the d03_epskin_lo/hi CGD and CTP CSVs (z=0 and z=0.4987), what are s_n+s_T and T/T500 at R500c? Is the change in M_HSE/M500 between eps_kin=0.02 and 1.2 smaller or larger than the d-01 redshift change (0.925 to 0.840)? And what f_nth(R500c) = 1 - M_HSE/M500 is needed for b=0?

Why does CPP (P/P500) have a much shallower slope than CGD x CTP beyond R500? At 2.05 R500, s_P = -2.88 against s_n+s_T = -4.25 at z=0, a 14 sigma difference. Is CPP a per-halo average of pressure (mean of products), a different weighting (volume- or mass-weighted), or a different halo sample, and which one is the right input for hydrostatic masses at r > R500?

dead_ends.why: The CGD/CTP/CPP emulators have no mass input. The only inputs are the 7 parameters kappa_w, e_w, M_seed, v_kin, epsilon_kin, omega_m and sigma_8, plus z. The output is one 19-bin profile in r/R500c (0.0154-2.74), with y = rho_gas/rho_crit and no mass column or mass bins, so each profile is for a single implicit (undocumented) cluster mass selection. issues.text: The calls do not fit the 13-call budget. Planned calls are list_observables, describe_parameters, 4 predict_observable, list_agent_files, up to 4 load_table_data, preview, describe, 2 overlays and 2 plot_prediction, which is about 18. Cut preview and describe_dataset, use one plot_prediction or none, and load only when outputs are files. Leave about 2 calls in reserve.

b_HSE needs a true mass, and that has to come from the emulator definition, not from assumption. Check whether CGD and CTP are stacked in M500c bins and whether radii are already scaled by the true R500c. If so, b_HSE at r = R500c(true) is well defined. If not, report only M_HSE(z_high)/M_HSE(z_low), as already planned. Also record whether CTP is mass-weighted, emission-weighted or spectroscopic. The bias differs by that choice, and FLAMINGO and X-COP use spectroscopic-like temperatures.

Check that 0.5, 1 and 2 R500c lie inside the emulator's radial range and grid. If 2 R500c is outside, say so rather than extrapolating. Differencing the upper and lower band edges does not give a valid slope uncertainty, because band edges are not correlated realisations. Label it a crude bound, or difference adjacent bins and report the spread. No tool computes derivatives, so show every input value and every step of the arithmetic so a reader can verify it.

list_observables reports a CPP (pressure) profile. Use d ln P/d ln r from CPP as an independent cross-check of s_n + s_T at both redshifts (2 extra predict calls; budget allowing). Without it the HSE slope rests on two separately emulated profiles whose errors may not be consistent.

Six fully cited papers with download, read and cite each takes about 18-20 calls, which is over budget. Fully cite 4 core papers: 2409.07849, 1805.00034 or 1805.00035, 1404.4636 and 2409.05815. Cover the rest with search_arxiv_abstracts and get_arxiv_metadata as abstract-level summaries, and do not cite them with quotes. get_paper_figures does not give citable verbatim text. Use at most one figure call.
Note that the emulator is HACC-based, not CAMELS (2010.00619), and FLAMINGO, Simba and HACC differ in subgrid models. Comparisons should be framed as qualitative trends, not one-to-one numbers.

This direction is over budget. It needs describe_parameters, 8 predicts, 2 or more fGas calls, loads and a plot, which exceeds 13. Reuse the d-01 fiducial outputs and run only the two feedback extremes at the two redshifts (8 predicts). Drop fGas unless calls remain, and drop the repeated list_observables. If the emulator has no explicit feedback parameters, stop and report that rather than substituting a cosmological parameter without saying so.

The 'required non-thermal fraction' depends on the true mass discussed under d-01. If the true mass is unavailable, compute only the f_nth-induced correction factor, using the Nelson f_nth(r, z) parameters from d-02. Mark any parameter that was not quoted in d-02 as unverified.

contested.reason: The CSV excerpts quoted as evidence (tc-35/37/38/39) show only the first six innermost bins (r < 0.09 R500c). The values used for the slopes at 0.49, 1.0 and 2.05 R500c, and T(R500)/T500 = 0.592 and 0.518, are not visible. d-04 independently reproduces only the z=0 density slope at R500 (-2.55). The arithmetic is internally consistent: 0.592*3.13/2 = 0.926, 0.518*3.24/2 = 0.839, and the stated errors follow from the slope errors. The interpretive part is not supported, however. (1) The quoted errors omit the T(R500) uncertainty. (2) The z=0 vs z=0.4987 difference in M_HSE/M500 is 0.085 +- 0.067 (about 1.3 sigma), so 'larger bias at higher z' is not significant. (3) Absolute b_HSE rests on an assumed T500 convention and an undocumented mass selection, which may differ between redshifts. (4) Treating bins as independent ignores GP covariance.

issues.text: The redshift change in M_HSE/M500 (0.925 vs 0.840) is about 1.3 sigma once errors are combined, and T(R500)/T500 errors are not propagated. The summary's statement that the larger bias at z=0.4987 comes from the 12% lower T(R500) needs a significance test before it enters the final discussion. Re-quote the actual bin values at 0.49, 1.0 and 2.05 R500c as evidence.

Sign convention mismatch. f-005 reports b_HSE as positive (1 - M_HSE/M), while FLAMINGO (f-001) uses (M_HSE - M)/M, which is negative. Harmonise the convention before comparing the two. Also note that if the profile stack uses a fixed mass threshold, the mean mass is lower at z=0.4987, so T/T500 and slope differences may partly reflect selection rather than evolution (q-06).

The critique c-01 suggestion to cross-check s_n + s_T against d ln P/d ln r from CPP was not done. Neither was a smooth-fit derivative (q-04). Finite differences of GP means with assumed independent errors are a weak basis for the 3.6-sigma s_T claim at 2 R500c.

The core difference (15-50% lower at z=0.4987) sits inside very large emulator errors. For example, at the innermost bin z=0.4987 gives 1018 +- 689 against 2154 +- 258 at z=0. It should be labelled not significant. The outer-radius percentages are not visible in the quoted excerpts, though the figures exist.

contested.reason: None of the quoted excerpts contains Eq. 7 or the values A=0.452, B=0.841, gamma=1.628. tc-68 shows only Figure 2/beta-axis text that mentions 'Eq 7', tc-60 shows the simulation section, and tc-79 only confirms that a citation was added. The arithmetic f_nth(0.5/0.55/0.6) = 0.254/0.274/0.294 does follow from the stated parameters. However, the R500c/R200m = 0.5-0.6 conversion is untooled hand arithmetic. It also ignores the emulator cosmology: omega_m=0.1375 is probably omega_m h^2, not Omega_m. For a typical NFW halo at z=0, R500c/R200m is closer to 0.45-0.5.

The method is incorrect. Including non-thermal pressure gives M_tot/M_HSE = [1/(1-f)] * [1 + (d ln(1/(1-f))/d ln r)/s_P], not the bare factor 1/(1-f). Because f_nth rises with radius, the bare factor overstates the correction, so the claimed '16-31% overcorrection' is inflated by construction. The same simplification sits behind the 'required f_nth ~ 1 - M_HSE/M500'. The finding also inherits the unverified parameters from f-009, and none of the cited evidence (two Nelson text chunks and two d-01 CTP CSVs) contains the derived numbers.

The only excerpt, tc-80 (chars 30000-45000), discusses cubic-spline scatter and the Barnes et al. comparison. It does not contain the -0.1 convergence in the 1e13.75-1e14.25 bin, the b=-0.257 calibration, the Fig. 2 weighting comparison or the Fig. 5 redshift statement. The quotes were not recorded with cite (d-06 admits this). The claims are plausible, but they are not supported by the quoted evidence.

Until the slopes and M_HSE/M500 are extracted for eps_kin=0.02 and 1.2, there is no evidence on whether Delta b(z) is larger or smaller than the feedback-induced spread. f-008 is supported only as a record of the runs.

The quoted CSV excerpts end at the first ~7 bins (r < 0.09 R500c), before the 0.365-2.738 R500c bins used for the slopes. The values are internally consistent: s_n+s_T reproduces d-01 exactly, and the errors add in quadrature correctly. Even so, the specific bin values should be quoted. The 14-sigma and 11-sigma CPP mismatch at 2.05 R500 is suspicious, as is the CPP slope at that radius flattening from -2.88 to -1.82 with z. Possible causes are

!= under halo-to-halo scatter or clumping, a different halo sample per emulator, or emulator edge effects near the 2.74 R500c grid boundary.

The 1.2-sigma significance treats GP errors as independent across bins and across redshifts. The z=0 and z=0.4987 predictions come from the same emulator, so correlated errors could raise or lower the significance substantially. Also, T(R500)/T500 = 0.59 is low compared with observed universal profiles (X-COP, roughly 0.8-0.9 at R500). This suggests that the emulator's T500 normalisation or temperature weighting differs from the kT500 = G mu m_p M500/(2R500) convention assumed. That would shift every absolute b value.
The FLAMINGO quotes still need to be recorded with cite. The X-COP 1805.00042 slope benchmark and the HACC documentation search (q-01, q-03, q-06) were not run.
